questions.q: What did the study of Finnish kindergarteners show about six-year-olds?
a: They already understood the importance of money
They preferred playing to earning money
They had no concept of prices yet
They copied spending habits from their parents
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the children discussed ticket prices and selling merchandise while putting on a play.

questions.q: What does the summary say about why managing money feels so hard?
a: Most people were never taught how to do it
Financial skills fade quickly without practice
Banks make budgeting deliberately confusing
Only people with high incomes can succeed
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the struggle is not a character flaw but a lack of proper financial teaching.

questions.q: What happened when berry pickers were paid by the number of baskets they filled?
a: Their productivity rose sharply
They began working more slowly
They quit to find other work
They earned less than before
questions.why: Lesson 2 says pay per basket boosted their incentive, unlike a simple raise.

questions.q: What did the study of journalism students find about payment and output?
a: Unpaid students wrote headlines twice as fast
Paid students produced better headlines
Both groups worked at the same pace
Unpaid students refused the assignment
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the students who received no money worked faster and joined more brainstorming sessions.

questions.q: What is hedonic adaptation, as described in the summary?
a: Getting used to pleasures that once felt exciting
Spending more as your income rises
Feeling guilt after buying something costly
Preferring saving over spending over time
questions.why: Lesson 3 says a treat becomes normal, so you seek bigger pleasures to feel satisfied.
